answer: Mechanism: Canyon-Ridge Beacon Scheduling. Each agent receives verifier-signed beacon times and must emit traffic as a ridge-shaped burst after a randomized canyon of silence; per-identity timing jitter is checked against neighboring agents. Sybils sharing a scheduler or host show correlated canyon boundaries and ridge slopes, so admission rejects clusters. An attacker must supply independent clocks, schedulers, and network paths per identity, multiplying per-sybil cost.
